words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.ex: She will lengthen the dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她会把裙子改长一点去参加派对。
words.en: To make something longer, or to become longer.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: The king was assassinated by a secret group.
words.ex_cn: 国王被一个秘密组织刺杀。
words.en: To assassinate someone means to murder them, especially for political reasons or for payment.

words.tr: v. 发芽；长出；迅速成长；涌现；
words.ex: The seed will sprout in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这颗种子会在春天发芽。
words.en: If a plant sprouts, or if it sprouts something, it produces new leaves or buds.

words.tr: n. 居住；生活环境；住所
words.ex: The old house has no habitation now.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子现在没有人居住。
words.en: The act of living in a place; a place where someone lives.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: He withdrew $100 from the ATM.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动取款机里提取了100美元。
words.en: If you withdraw something from a place, you remove it or take it away.

words.tr:
n. 撤退；退却；静居处；
v. 撤退；退却；
words.ex: The army ordered a retreat after the battle.
words.ex_cn: 战斗后，军队下令撤退。
words.en: If you retreat, you move away from something or someone, often because you are frightened or because you want to be alone. A retreat is also a quiet, isolated place that you go to in order to rest or to do things in private.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.tr:
adj. 明白表示的；证实的；公然表示情绪的
n. 指示词
words.ex: He is demonstrative with his love for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他对家人表达爱意时很外露。
words.en: If you are demonstrative, you show your feelings or behave in a way that shows your love for someone.

words.ex: They equally share the housework.
words.ex_cn: 他们同样分担家务。
words.en: In a manner that is the same in amount, degree, or value.

words.ex: He deliberately broke the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他有意地违反了规则。
words.en: If you do something deliberately, you do it intentionally or after thinking about it carefully.

words.tr: v. 影响；“affect”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 染病的；受感动的；
words.ex: The rain affected the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨影响了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as affected, you disapprove of the fact that they behave in an unnatural way that is intended to impress other people.

words.ex: He eats cereal with milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃谷类食品配牛奶。
words.en: A cereal is a grass that is cultivated for the edible components of its grain, composed of the endosperm, germ, and bran.

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.ex: He took the chairmanship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年担任了主席职务。
words.en: The position or period of being a chairman, especially of a committee or board.

words.ex: The children played near the cinder pile after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在火堆后的煤渣堆旁玩耍。
words.en: A cinder is a small piece of partly burnt coal or wood that has stopped giving off flames but still has combustible matter in it.

words.ex: This room is comparatively small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间相对较小。
words.en: In comparison with something else, especially something similar; relatively.

words.ex: The comparison of the two phones helped me decide.
words.ex_cn: 对这两部手机的比较帮助我做出了决定。
words.en: When you make a comparison, you consider two or more things and discover the differences or similarities between them.

words.tr: adj. 迷惑的；混乱的； v. 迷惑；混淆；“confuse”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He looked confused when the teacher asked the question.
words.ex_cn: 老师问问题时，他看起来很迷惑。
words.en: If you are confused, you do not know exactly what is happening or what to do.

words.ex: He showed courtesy by holding the door open.
words.ex_cn: 他为别人扶着门，表现得很礼貌。
words.en: Courtesy is polite behavior, or a polite action or remark.

words.ex: The storm caused disastrous damage to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给村庄造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as disastrous, you mean that it is very unfortunate or unsuccessful.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.tr:
n. 纪录片；
adj. 文书的；
words.ex: We watched a documentary about pandas last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于熊猫的纪录片。
words.en: A documentary is a film or television or radio programme that gives factual information about a particular subject.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: The package arrived at my doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 包裹送到我家门口了。
words.en: A doorstep is a step in front of an outer door to a building.

words.ex: He is doubtless the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是队里最好的球员。
words.en: used to say that something is almost certain or very likely

words.ex: The king's greed led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 国王的贪婪导致了他的没落。
words.en: The collapse of a person or organization's power, status, or success.

words.tr: n. 低迷时期；衰退；下滑；
words.ex: Many businesses struggled during the economic downturn.
words.ex_cn: 许多企业在经济低迷时期挣扎求生。
words.en: A downturn is a period of time in which something such as business activity, production, or investment decreases or becomes worse.

words.ex: The rainwater drains into the street.
words.ex_cn: 雨水排入街道。
words.en: If you drain something, you remove the liquid from it, usually by pouring it away or by allowing it to flow away. If something drains, the liquid flows away from it.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.tr: n. 梦想家；空想家；不切实际的人；
words.ex: He is a dreamer who wants to change the world.
words.ex_cn: 他是个想要改变世界的人。
words.en: A dreamer is someone who has a lot of ideas and plans for the future but is not practical or realistic about them.

words.ex: The extent of his knowledge surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识广度让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The area or length to which something extends.

words.tr: adj. 有缺陷的；有故障的；有错误的；
words.ex: The faulty phone keeps turning off.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺陷的手机总是自动关机。
words.en: If you describe something as faulty, you mean that it is not perfect or it has some weaknesses.

words.ex: The children threw garbage on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们把垃圾扔在地上。
words.en: Waste material; unwanted or undesired material.

words.ex: The geologist studied rocks in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这位地质学家研究了山里的岩石。
words.en: A geologist is a scientist who studies the solid, liquid, and gaseous matter that constitutes the Earth and other terrestrial planets, as well as the processes that shape them.

words.ex: She walked with grace across the stage.
words.ex_cn: 她优雅地走过舞台。
words.en: Grace is the quality of being pleasant, polite, and dignified, or a period of time allowed for something to be done.

words.ex: The ship docked at the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船停靠在海港。
words.en: A harbor is a place on the coast where ships may moor in shelter, especially one protected from rough water by piers, jetties, and other artificial structures.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.ex: The old ship was a monster on the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船在海上是个庞然大物。
words.en: A monster is an imaginary creature that is very large, ugly, and frightening.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.ex: A moth flew into the room through the window.
words.ex_cn: 一只蛾子从窗户飞进了房间。
words.en: A moth is an insect with wings that is related to the butterfly. Moths are often attracted to light and are mostly active at night.

words.ex: The oncoming storm made everyone hurry home.
words.ex_cn: 即将到来的风暴让所有人都赶紧回家。
words.en: An oncoming thing is moving towards you and is likely to reach you or affect you soon.

words.ex: This phone is outdated and doesn't work well.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了，用起来不好。
words.en: If you describe something as outdated, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr:
v. 包装；收拾行李；
n. 包裹；小包；
words.ex: She packs the gift in colorful paper.
words.ex_cn: 她用彩纸包装礼物。
words.en: A pack is a container of a particular kind, especially one made of strong paper or plastic and containing a number of the same items. As a verb, pack means to put something into a container, especially in a neat and efficient way.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；实际的；实践的；
words.ex: This tool is practical for everyday use.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具日常使用很实用。
words.en: relating to what is real rather than to what is possible or imagined; likely to succeed or be effective in real circumstances; involving or concerned with experience or actual use; not theoretical

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.tr:
v. 滚动；
n. 滚动；卷形物；
words.ex: The ball roll down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 球从山上滚下来。
words.en: To move somewhere by turning over and over, or to make something move in this way.

words.ex: The seismic wave shook the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震波震动了地面。
words.en: Seismic means relating to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration.

words.ex: He walks on the sidewalk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在人行道上走路。
words.en: A sidewalk is a path with a hard surface by the side of a road that people walk on.

words.ex: He bought a sizable house with a big garden.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一所很大的房子，带一个大花园。
words.en: Something that is sizable is fairly large.

words.ex: He has a slight cold.
words.ex_cn: 他有点轻微的感冒。
words.en: A slight change, difference, or action is not very great or important.

words.ex: The submarine sailed quietly under the sea.
words.ex_cn: 潜水艇在海底安静地航行。
words.en: A submarine is a type of ship that can travel underwater. It is used primarily by the military for defense purposes, but some are used for scientific research.

words.ex: He is a supporter of the local team.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地球队的支持者。
words.en: A supporter is someone who supports a particular person, group, or cause.

words.tr: n. 损失；伤亡人数；通行费；
words.ex: The war caused a heavy toll on innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 战争给平民带来了巨大的损失。
words.en: A toll is a small sum of money that you have to pay in order to use a particular bridge or road. / A toll is the total number of deaths, accidents, or disasters that occur in a particular period of time. / When a bell tolls, it rings slowly and repeatedly, often as a sign that someone has died.

words.tr: adj. 不适宜的；不合适的；
words.ex: This shirt is unsuitable for the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫不适合寒冷的天气。
words.en: If someone or something is unsuitable for a particular purpose or situation, they are not appropriate for it.

words.ex: He was utterly surprised by the news.
words.ex_cn: 他全然没想到这个消息。
words.en: completely or totally

words.ex: He is constantly checking his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他不断地查看他的手机。
words.en: If something happens constantly, it happens all the time or very often.

words.tr:
adj. 未知的；不为人知的；
n. 未知的地方（或事物）；
words.ex: The unknown cause of the accident is being investigated.
words.ex_cn: 事故的未知原因正在调查中。
words.en: If something is unknown, it is not known or recognized by people.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；瞬间的；刹那间的
words.ex: The light made a momentary flash.
words.ex_cn: 灯光闪了一下，但只持续了一瞬间。
words.en: lasting for a very short time

words.ex: The aboriginal people live in the forests of Australia.
words.ex_cn: 土著居民生活在澳大利亚的森林里。
words.en: An aboriginal person or thing is one that has been in a country or region from the earliest known times or from before the arrival of colonists.

words.ex: The weather was tolerable, so we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气还可以忍受，所以我们去散步了。
words.en: If something is tolerable, it is acceptable or bearable, even though it is not very good or pleasant.

words.ex: Eating too much sugar is unhealthy.
words.ex_cn: 吃太多糖是不健康的。
words.en: If you describe something as unhealthy, you mean that it is likely to cause illness or poor health.

words.tr: adj. 不公平的；非正义的
words.ex: The judge made an unjust decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个不公正的决定。
words.en: If you describe an action, system, or law as unjust, you think that it treats a person or group badly in a way that they do not deserve.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: The abolition of slavery took many years.
words.ex_cn: 废除奴隶制花了许多年。
words.en: The act of officially ending or stopping something, such as a system, practice, or institution.

words.ex: His rude comment was a provocation to start a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论是一种挑衅，想引发争斗。
words.en: If you describe someone's action as a provocation, you mean that it is likely to cause a reaction or argument, especially a violent or angry one.

words.tr:
adj. 唯一的；
n. 鞋底；
words.ex: He is the sole owner of the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家商店唯一的主人。
words.en: If you describe something as the sole thing of a particular kind, you mean that it is the only one of that kind.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.ex: She smiled subtly when she heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 她听到这个消息时微妙地笑了。
words.en: In a way that is so delicate or precise as to be difficult to analyze or describe.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.ex: The editor abridged the long story for children.
words.ex_cn: 编辑删节了这个长故事，以便适合儿童阅读。
words.en: To abridge a book, play, or other text means to make it shorter by leaving parts out.

words.ex: The fire blackened the pot.
words.ex_cn: 火把锅烧黑了。
words.en: To make or become black or dark, especially by the action of fire, smoke, or dirt; to defame someone's character.

words.ex: The king was sent into exile after the revolution.
words.ex_cn: 革命后，国王被流放了。
words.en: Exile is the state of being sent away from one's home country or place of residence, often for political or punitive reasons.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the pigs to fatten them.
words.ex_cn: 农夫喂猪使它们长胖。
words.en: To make or become fat or fatter.

words.ex: He gave her flattery to make her happy.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承她，让她开心。
words.en: Flattery is the act of praising someone in an insincere way in order to make them feel good or to get something from them.

words.ex: His folly led to the loss of his job.
words.ex_cn: 他的愚蠢导致他丢了工作。
words.en: If you say that a particular action or way of behaving is folly, you mean that it is foolish.

words.tr:
adj. 专横的；爱发号施令的
n. 母牛或小牛
words.ex: She is bossy and tells others what to do.
words.ex_cn: 她很专横，总是告诉别人该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as bossy, you mean that they enjoy telling people what to do.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: He is learning the English alphabet.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习英文字母。
words.en: An alphabet is a set of letters or symbols in a fixed order used for writing a language.

words.ex: He uses a calculator to add numbers.
words.ex_cn: 他用计算器来加数字。
words.en: A calculator is a small electronic device that you use for doing mathematical calculations.

words.ex: He carved the meat with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用一把锋利的刀切开了肉。
words.en: To carve means to cut into a hard material in order to produce an object, design, or inscription.

words.tr:
n. 芯片；
v. 削成碎片；碎裂；
words.ex: The computer chip is very small.
words.ex_cn: 计算机芯片非常小。
words.en: A chip is a small piece which has been broken off something larger, or a small piece of silicon used to make computer parts.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.ex: The teacher drew a diagram to explain the water cycle.
words.ex_cn: 老师画了一个图表来解释水循环。
words.en: A diagram is a simple drawing which consists mainly of lines and is used, for example, to explain how a machine works.

words.tr:
n. 水滴
v. 滴落
words.ex: The tap is dripping slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头在慢慢滴水。
words.en: If a liquid drips, it falls in small drops. A drip is also a small amount of liquid that falls in this way.

words.tr:
v. 下毛毛雨；（毛毛雨似的）洒落
n. 毛毛细雨
words.ex: It is drizzling outside.
words.ex_cn: 外面正在下毛毛雨。
words.en: Light rain falling in very fine drops.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: He is a fast eater.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吃饭很快的人。
words.en: A person or animal that consumes food.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.ex: He tries to economize by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省开支。
words.en: To economize means to use less money, time, or resources than usual in order to save them.

words.ex: The elderly man walks slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位年老的男子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: An elderly person is someone who is old or aging.

words.ex: He is learning elementary math at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习初级数学。
words.en: Elementary means relating to the simplest and most basic aspects of a subject.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: He showed strong emotion when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，表现出了强烈的情绪。
words.en: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.tr: v. 使全神贯注；独占；垄断
words.ex: He is engrossed in reading a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他正全神贯注地读一本小说。
words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.tr: n. 入会；入学 ；登记；注册；加入人数
words.ex: His enrollment in the club was approved last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周被批准加入该俱乐部。
words.en: The act of officially joining a course, school, etc., or the number of people who do this.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.ex: The old estate has large gardens and a beautiful mansion.
words.ex_cn: 这个古老的庄园有大片花园和一座美丽的豪宅。
words.en: An estate is all the money and property that someone owns, especially everything that is left when they die.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.tr: adj. 永久的；永恒的；经久不变的
words.ex: The love between them is everlasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是永恒的。
words.en: Something that is everlasting lasts forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: The weather is exceedingly cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气极其寒冷。
words.en: To a very great degree; extremely.

words.ex: He eats excessively sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多甜食。
words.en: To an excessive degree; more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; inordinately.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.tr:
v. 豁免；
adj. 被免除的；
words.ex: The school exempted him from the test.
words.ex_cn: 学校免除了他的考试。
words.en: If someone or something is exempt from a particular rule, duty, or obligation, they do not have to follow it or do it.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr: adj. 有才智的；聪明的；明智的；
words.ex: The intelligent boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个有才智的男孩很快解出了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is intelligent has the ability to think, understand, and learn things quickly and well.

words.tr:
n. 魔术；魔法；
adj. 魔术（似）的；神奇的；
words.ex: He performed magic at the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 他在生日聚会上表演了魔术。
words.en: Magic is the power to use supernatural forces to make impossible things happen, such as making people disappear or controlling events in nature.

words.ex: He hammered the nail into the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他把钉子敲进了木头里。
words.en: A nail is a thin pointed piece of metal that is hammered into materials as a fastener. It can also refer to the hard covering at the end of fingers and toes. As a verb, to nail means to fasten something with a nail or to catch or accomplish something successfully.

words.tr: v. 代表；表现；体现；相当于；
words.ex: He represents his country in the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中代表他的国家。
words.en: If someone represents a person or group of people, they act on behalf of that person or group.

words.ex: The scene at the park was peaceful.
words.ex_cn: 公园里的场景很宁静。
words.en: A scene is a part of a play or film in which the action stays in one place for a continuous period of time.

words.ex: The phone has a silicon chip inside.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机内部有一个硅芯片。
words.en: Silicon is a chemical element with the symbol Si and atomic number 14. It is a hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic lustre, and is a tetravalent metalloid and semiconductor.

words.tr:
n. 长条；条状；
v. 剥去；剥夺；
words.ex: He cut a strip of paper to wrap the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他剪了一条纸来包装礼物。
words.en: To remove a layer from something, or to take off your clothes.

words.tr: v. 工作；劳动；“work”的现在分词； adj. 工作的；劳动的；
words.ex: He is working in a factory.
words.ex_cn: 他正在工厂工作。
words.en: Engaged in work, especially as one's regular occupation; functioning or able to function.

words.tr: n. 大片土地；体内管道；
words.ex: The farmer owns a large tract of land near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有靠近河边的一大片土地。
words.en: A tract is a large area of land or a system of connected organs in the body.

words.ex: The trainee is learning how to use the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这位受训者正在学习如何使用这台机器。
words.en: A trainee is someone who is being taught how to do a particular job.

words.tr: n. 运输；运输系统；交通工具；
words.ex: The city improved its transportation system.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了它的运输系统。
words.en: Transportation refers to the movement of people, animals, and goods from one place to another.

words.ex: The troupe performed a dance show in the town square.
words.ex_cn: 这个表演团在广场上演了一出舞蹈表演。
words.en: A troupe is a group of actors, singers, or dancers who work together.

words.ex: He is a trustworthy friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone as trustworthy, you mean they are reliable, honest, and truthful.

words.ex: He is truthful when he speaks about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 当他谈论自己的错误时，他是诚实的。
words.en: If someone is truthful, they tell the truth and do not lie.

words.tr: adv. 灵活地；柔软地；有弹性地；
words.ex: She adapts flexibly to new situations.
words.ex_cn: 她能灵活地适应新情况。
words.en: In a way that is able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: He vaguely remembered the name.
words.ex_cn: 他模糊地记得这个名字。
words.en: If you describe something as vaguely, you mean that it is not clear, distinct, or definite.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.tr: adj. 诡诈的；诡秘的；心照不宣的
words.ex: The sly fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is sly is clever and good at deceiving people in a way that is not easily noticed.

words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is inappropriate.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去参加会议是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that something is inappropriate, you are criticizing it because you think it is not suitable for a particular situation or purpose.

words.tr: adv. 公认地；普遍承认地；诚然；
words.ex: Admittedly, he is not the best player, but he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 公认地，他不是最好的球员，但他很努力。
words.en: Used to express that you accept something is true or that you agree with it, even though you may not like it.

words.ex: The movie shows a supernatural ghost.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个超自然的幽灵。
words.en: Relating to phenomena that cannot be explained by natural laws and are therefore attributed to a divine agency.

words.tr:
v. 使不再抱幻想；使理想破灭
n. 幻灭；理想破灭
words.ex: The bad experience disillusioned him about politics.
words.ex_cn: 这次糟糕的经历让他对政治不再抱幻想。
words.en: If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought it was.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: The teacher asked us to dissect the poem line by line.
words.ex_cn: 老师让我们逐行仔细分析这首诗。
words.en: To dissect something means to cut it into pieces in order to examine its structure, or to study something in great detail.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.ex: The monster made a monstrous sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物发出了巨大的声音。
words.en: If you describe something as monstrous, you mean that it is extremely large or that it is extremely unpleasant or wrong.

words.ex: He is a sociable man who likes to talk with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢和朋友聊天的外向的人。
words.en: A sociable person is friendly and enjoys being with other people.

words.ex: He sang a mournful song at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上唱了一首悲伤的歌。
words.en: If you are mournful, you are very sad.

words.ex: The company plans to diversify its products.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划使产品多样化。
words.en: To diversify means to make or become more varied or different. It often refers to the process of a company or individual expanding their range of products or activities to reduce risk or to explore new opportunities.

words.tr: v. 改编为戏剧；渲染；使戏剧化
words.ex: They dramatize the novel for the stage.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这部小说改编成舞台剧。
words.en: If a book or story is dramatized, it is written or presented as a play, film, or television drama.

words.ex: He works on an advisory committee.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个顾问委员会工作。
words.en: An advisory is a report or announcement that gives advice or information about a particular subject.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: The house has a small annex for storage.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个用于存放物品的小附属物。
words.en: To annex means to take control of a country, region, etc., especially by force; to add an area or region to a country, state, etc. : to take control of (a territory or place).

words.ex: The Philippines is an archipelago of thousands of islands.
words.ex_cn: 菲律宾是一个由数千个岛屿组成的群岛。
words.en: An archipelago is a group of islands, especially small islands, scattered in a body of water.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: The accident was avoidable if he had slowed down.
words.ex_cn: 如果他减速了，这场事故本可以避免。
words.en: If something is avoidable, it can be prevented or not done.

words.tr:
n. 大楼；大厦；块；街区；障碍物；
v. 阻塞；阻碍；
words.ex: The new block is next to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这栋新大楼就在公园旁边。
words.en: A block is a large solid piece of material with flat surfaces on each side. As a verb, to block means to prevent movement or progress.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.ex: The connection between the two wires is loose.
words.ex_cn: 两根电线之间的连接松了。
words.en: A connection is a relationship between two things, people, or groups.

words.ex: The queen wore a golden crown on her head.
words.ex_cn: 女王头上戴着一顶金皇冠。
words.en: A crown is a circular ornament, usually made of gold and jewels, which a king or queen wears on their head at official ceremonies. It can also refer to the top part of something, such as a tooth or a hill, or to the act of making someone a king or queen by placing a crown on their head.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: The establishment of the school took five years.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的建立花了五年时间。
words.en: The act of establishing something or the state of being established. It can also refer to an organization or institution, especially a business or public body.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.ex: He has eyestrain from looking at his phone too long.
words.ex_cn: 他因为长时间看手机而眼睛疲劳。
words.en: Eyestrain is a condition in which the eyes get tired from being used too much, especially for activities that require intense focus, such as reading or computer work.

words.ex: The colors of the painting fade in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的颜色在阳光下逐渐消失。
words.en: To gradually grow faint and disappear.

words.ex: The faint light from the candle barely lit the room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛微弱的光几乎照不亮房间。
words.en: If you feel faint, you feel weak and as if you are about to lose consciousness. Something that is faint is not strong or clear.

words.ex: His familiarity with the city helped him find the way.
words.ex_cn: 他对这座城市的熟悉帮助他找到了路。
words.en: A thorough knowledge or mastery of a subject, place, or situation, often gained through experience.

words.ex: He wants to familiarize himself with the new software.
words.ex_cn: 他想熟悉这个新软件。
words.en: To familiarize someone with something means to give them knowledge or experience of it.

words.ex: Please fetch me a glass of water.
words.ex_cn: 请给我拿一杯水来。
words.en: If you fetch something or someone, you go to the place where they are and return with them.

words.ex: He eats fiber to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃纤维来保持健康。
words.en: A fiber is a thread or a structure or object resembling a thread, especially one that is used to make cloth or rope.

words.ex: He loves reading science fiction.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读科幻小说。
words.en: Fiction refers to literature in the form of prose, especially novels, that describes imaginary events and people.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.ex: The farmer owns five hectares of land.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有五公顷土地。
words.en: A hectare is a unit of measurement of area, equal to 10,000 square metres or approximately 2.471 acres.

words.ex: The homeless man slept on the bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个无家可归的人睡在长椅上。
words.en: If someone is homeless, they have no permanent place to live.

words.ex: The jury decided the man was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团裁定这个人无罪。
words.en: A jury is a group of people who are chosen to decide whether someone is guilty or not guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The minority group voted for change.
words.ex_cn: 少数群体投票支持变革。
words.en: A minority is a group of people within a community or country who are different from the majority of the people there in race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.ex: The opposition to the new law was strong.
words.ex_cn: 对这项新法律的反对很强烈。
words.en: Opposition is strong disagreement with or resistance to something, especially a plan, policy, or government.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: This job requires patience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作需要耐心。
words.en: If you require something, you need it or want it.

words.ex: His sentiment about the new policy is positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对新政策的看法是积极的。
words.en: A sentiment is a thought, opinion, or idea based on a feeling about a situation, or a way of thinking about something.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.ex: The country values its sovereignty.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家重视它的主权。
words.en: Sovereignty is the power that a country has to govern itself or another country or state.

words.tr:
n. 时距；跨度；
v. 跨越；
words.ex: The span of his career was 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的时距是40年。
words.en: The extent or measure of space between two points or extremities, as of a bridge or a roof; the full extent, stretch, or reach of anything.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: adv. 自愿地；自动地；主动地；
words.ex: He voluntarily helped the old man cross the street.
words.ex_cn: 他自愿帮助那位老人过马路。
words.en: If you do something voluntarily, you do it willingly, without being forced to do it.

words.ex: The boxes are stored in the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 这些箱子存放在仓库里。
words.en: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods may be stored before their export or distribution for sale.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: Please don't disturb me while I'm reading.
words.ex_cn: 我读书时请不要打扰我。
words.en: To disturb someone means to interrupt what they are doing and cause them inconvenience or annoyance.

words.tr: v. 缠住；“dog”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The reporter dogged the politician everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 记者紧紧跟随这位政治家到处。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as dogged, you mean that they are determined to continue with something even if it becomes difficult or dangerous.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: The diary entries were fragmentary and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这些日记条目是不完整的，难以理解。
words.en: Consisting of small parts that are disconnected or incomplete.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；高傲自大的
words.ex: He gave a haughty smile when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品时露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as haughty, you mean that they behave in a proud, unfriendly way, because they think that they are better than other people.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；思想上的桎梏
v. 用手铐铐住（某人）；把（某人）铐在（某物、某人）上；限制
words.ex: The police put handcuff on the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察给小偷戴上了手铐。
words.en: A handcuff is a pair of lockable linked metal rings for securing a prisoner's wrists.

words.ex: The headman led his tribe to find new land.
words.ex_cn: 酋长带领他的部落寻找新土地。
words.en: A headman is the leader or chief of a village or tribe.

words.ex: He felt anxiety before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到忧虑。
words.en: Anxiety is a feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.tr:
n. 接触；联系；
v. 接触；联系；
words.ex: The two balls made contact when they collided.
words.ex_cn: 两个球在碰撞时发生了接触。
words.en: Contact refers to the act of communicating with someone, especially regularly, or the state of touching something.

words.tr:
n. 内容；含量；
adj. 满足的；
words.ex: The content of the video is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这个视频的内容非常有趣。
words.en: Content refers to the things that are held or included in something, or the state of being happy and satisfied.

words.ex: He waited for hours, and eventually got his turn.
words.ex_cn: 他等了几个小时，终于轮到他了。
words.en: At an unspecified later time; in the end.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: The fluorescent lamp lights up the room quickly.
words.ex_cn: 荧光灯很快照亮了房间。
words.en: Fluorescent substances produce bright light of a particular color when they are exposed to light of a different wavelength.

words.ex: The footbridge connects the two sides of the river.
words.ex_cn: 这座人行桥连接了河的两岸。
words.en: A footbridge is a narrow bridge for pedestrians.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: Steve Jobs is the founder of Apple.
words.ex_cn: 史蒂夫·乔布斯是苹果公司的创办者。
words.en: A founder is someone who establishes an organization, company, or institution. As a verb, it means to fail or collapse, especially in terms of a plan or a ship sinking.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.ex: The flower has a sweet fragrance.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有一种甜美的香味。
words.en: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, especially that of a flower or perfume.

words.ex: He is a guru in computer programming.
words.ex_cn: 他是计算机编程方面的专家。
words.en: A guru is a person who is very skilled and knowledgeable in a particular subject, and who gives advice and guidance to others.

words.ex: He is frugal with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很节俭。
words.en: If you describe someone as frugal, you mean that they are careful about spending money and use things only when they need to.

words.tr: adj. 无结果的；无成效的；
words.ex: The meeting was fruitless because no decisions were made.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议毫无结果，因为没有做出任何决定。
words.en: If an action or attempt to do something is fruitless, it is unsuccessful or produces nothing of value.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.tr:
n. 一群；一帮；一伙
v. 成群结队；结成一伙；合伙攻击
words.ex: The gang stole a car last night.
words.ex_cn: 那群人昨晚偷了一辆车。
words.en: A gang is a group of people, especially young people, who go around together and often deliberately cause trouble.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.tr: adv. 高兴地；乐意地；欣然地；
words.ex: She gladly helped her friend with homework.
words.ex_cn: 她高兴地帮朋友做作业。
words.en: If you do something gladly, you do it willingly and with pleasure.

words.ex: She took a glance at the clock.
words.ex_cn: 她瞥了一眼钟。
words.en: If you glance at something or someone, you look at them very quickly and then look away again immediately.

words.ex: The glare of the sun made it hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 阳光的刺眼使我看不清。
words.en: If you glare at someone, you look at them with an angry expression on your face. Glare is also a very bright light that is uncomfortable to look at.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.ex: I caught a glimpse of the cat before it ran away.
words.ex_cn: 我在它跑掉之前瞥了一眼那只猫。
words.en: A glimpse is a brief, quick look at something or someone.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.ex: He grabbed the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速抓住了球。
words.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

words.ex: The gardener did a graft on the apple tree.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在苹果树上进行了嫁接。
words.en: Graft can refer to the act of joining parts from different plants so that they grow as one plant, or to the act of transferring living tissue from one part of the body to another. It can also refer to the practice of using one's position to gain money or advantages dishonestly.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.tr:
n. 紧握；掌握；控制；
v. 紧握；掌握；
words.ex: He has a strong grip on the handle.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握住把手。
words.en: To grip something means to hold it tightly. It can also mean to hold someone's attention completely.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.tr:
n. 冰雹；
v. 把…誉为；
words.ex: The hail broke many car windows.
words.ex_cn: 冰雹打碎了许多汽车窗户。
words.en: Hail is small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky. It can also mean to call out to someone in order to attract their attention, or to praise someone enthusiastically.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.ex: He is literate and can read simple books.
words.ex_cn: 他有读写能力，能读简单的书。
words.en: A literate person is able to read and write, and has a good education.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.tr:
n. 反面；对立面；
adj. 对面的；
prep. 与…相对；
words.ex: The opposite of black is white.
words.ex_cn: 黑色的反面是白色。
words.en: If one thing is opposite another, it is on the other side of a space from it.

words.tr: adj. 正确的；合适的；正当的；
words.ex: This is the proper way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是解决这个问题的正确方法。
words.en: If something is proper, it is suitable or correct for a particular purpose, situation, or person.

words.tr:
n. 请求；要求的事；
v. 要求；请求；
words.ex: He made a request for help.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个帮助的请求。
words.en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.

words.tr: n. 学校作业；课堂作业；
words.ex: He finished his schoolwork before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚饭前完成了学校作业。
words.en: Schoolwork refers to the work that students are required to do as part of their studies at school.

words.tr: n. 一段时间；会议；会期；开庭；学年；
words.ex: We had a long session of studying together.
words.ex_cn: 我们一起学习了一段时间。
words.en: A session is a meeting of a court, parliament, or other official group, or a period of time used for a particular activity, especially by a group of people.

words.tr:
n. 调查；勘测；
v. 调查；勘测；
words.ex: The school did a survey about student lunch preferences.
words.ex_cn: 学校做了一项关于学生午餐偏好的调查。
words.en: A survey is a detailed study or inspection, especially as a means of collecting information about people's opinions or behavior.

words.ex: His behavior is unacceptable.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为是不可接受的。
words.en: If you describe something as unacceptable, you strongly disapprove of it or object to it and feel that it should not be allowed to continue.

words.tr: adj. 无人照料的；无人看管的；
words.ex: The unattended child cried near the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个无人照料的孩子在公园长椅旁哭了。
words.en: If something is unattended, there is nobody looking after it or taking care of it.

words.tr:
adj. 解开的
v. 解开；“unbind”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The dog ran unbound across the field.
words.ex_cn: 狗无拘无束地跑过田野。
words.en: If something is unbound, it is not tied or held together by anything, or it is not restricted or limited by rules or laws.

words.tr: adj. 无意识的；无知觉的；
words.ex: He was unconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了意识。
words.en: If someone is unconscious, they are not awake, usually because they have had a severe injury or illness.

words.tr: n. 人事不省；意识丧失
words.ex: He fell into unconsciousness after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了意识。
words.en: The state of being unaware of and unable to respond to one's surroundings.

words.ex: The fire became uncontrollable after the wind blew strongly.
words.ex_cn: 风猛烈吹起后，火势变得无法控制。
words.en: If something is uncontrollable, it cannot be controlled or managed.

words.ex: The country has an underdeveloped economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经济不发达。
words.en: An underdeveloped country or region is one that is less developed economically and socially than most others, with many of its people living in poverty.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；大量的；辽阔的；
words.ex: The desert is vast and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠巨大而空旷。
words.en: If you describe something as vast, you mean that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 血淋淋的；嗜杀的；残暴的
words.ex: The battle was known for its sanguinary nature.
words.ex_cn: 这场战斗因其血腥的性质而闻名。
words.en: Involving or causing much bloodshed; marked by great slaughter.

words.tr:
n. 刺穿；刺孔
v. 刺穿；削弱
words.ex: The bike tire has a puncture.
words.ex_cn: 自行车轮胎有一个漏气孔。
words.en: A puncture is a small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To puncture something means to make a hole in it with a sharp object.

words.tr:
v. 睡眠
n. 睡眠（常复数）
words.ex: The baby fell into a deep slumber after feeding.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝喂完奶后进入了深深的睡眠。
words.en: Slumber is a state of sleep, especially one that is peaceful and restful.

words.ex: The sun scorch the ground in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光灼烧地面。
words.en: To burn the surface of something so as to discolour or damage it.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.tr:
v. 扭伤
n. 扭伤
words.ex: He sprained his ankle while running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时扭伤了脚踝。
words.en: If you sprain a joint such as your ankle or wrist, you accidentally damage it by twisting it or bending it violently.

words.tr:
v. 洒；撒；下小雨
n. 洒；撒；小雨；少量
words.ex: She sprinkles sugar on her cereal.
words.ex_cn: 她在麦片上撒糖。
words.en: To scatter or pour small drops or particles of a substance over an object or surface.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.ex: The city's skyline looks beautiful at night.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的天际线在夜晚看起来很美。
words.en: The outline of land and buildings defined against the sky.

words.tr: adj. 有军人气质的；英武的
words.ex: His actions were marked by soldierly courage and discipline.
words.ex_cn: 他的行动体现了军人的勇气和纪律。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or appearance as soldierly, you mean that they behave or look like a soldier, especially in being brave, disciplined, or smart.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.tr: v. 分类；“classify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The librarian classified the books by subject.
words.ex_cn: 图书管理员按主题对书籍进行分类。
words.en: Officially designated as secret and accessible only to authorized personnel.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.ex: The fence encircles the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏围绕着花园。
words.en: To encircle something or someone means to surround them completely.

words.tr: v. 提前；前进；“advance”的现在分词； adj. 前进的；
words.ex: He is advancing the meeting to Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他把会议提前到周一。
words.en: To move forward or make progress, especially in a purposeful way.

words.ex: The food was appallingly bad.
words.ex_cn: 这食物糟糕得令人震惊。
words.en: In a way that causes shock or dismay; extremely.

words.tr: adv. 显然；表面上看起来；
words.ex: He is apparently late for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他显然迟到了会议。
words.en: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard, but you are not certain that it is true.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.ex: She is an attractive woman.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有吸引力的女性。
words.en: An attractive person or thing is pleasing or appealing to look at.

words.tr: n. 就寝时间；睡觉时间；
words.ex: His bedtime is 9 p.m. every night.
words.ex_cn: 他的就寝时间是每天晚上9点。
words.en: The time when someone usually goes to bed.

words.ex: The fence marks the boundary between the two gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏标志着两个花园的分界线。
words.en: A boundary is a real or imagined line that marks the edge or limit of something.

words.tr: adj. 有挑战性的； v. 提出挑战；“challenge”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math problem was challenging.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题很有挑战性。
words.en: If you describe something as challenging, you mean that it tests your ability and determination and that you need to work hard to deal with it or achieve it.

words.tr: n. 殖民者；殖民地居民；移民
words.ex: The colonist built a small house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位殖民者在河边建了一座小房子。
words.en: A colonist is a person who settles in a new colony or moves to live in a new country.

words.ex: He gave careful consideration to his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的决定进行了仔细考虑。
words.en: Consideration is the process of giving careful thought to something before making a decision or taking action. It also refers to the quality of being thoughtful towards the needs and feelings of others.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 漂移；
words.ex: The drift of the river carries leaves downstream.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流动将树叶冲向下游。
words.en: If something or someone drifts somewhere, they move there slowly or gradually. As a noun, drift can refer to a slow, gradual movement or change, or the general meaning or intent of something.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: The evolution of birds from dinosaurs took millions of years.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类从恐龙进化而来花了数百万年。
words.en: The gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr: adj. 有收益的；有报酬的；有利可图的
words.ex: He found a gainful job after graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他毕业后找到了一份有收入的工作。
words.en: Providing gain; profitable.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；努力工作的
words.ex: He is hard-working and always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他很勤奋，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is hard-working always puts a lot of effort and care into their work.

words.tr:
v. 共享；分享；
n. 分享；股份；
words.ex: They share their food with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他们与朋友分享食物。
words.en: If you share something with another person, you both have it, use it, or are involved in it. You can also say that two people share something.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 马具；
words.ex: We must harness the power of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须利用太阳的能量。
words.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten round their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.tr:
n. 婴儿；
adj. 初期的；
words.ex: The infant is sleeping in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在婴儿床里睡觉。
words.en: An infant is a baby or very young child.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.ex: Pop music is part of the mainstream.
words.ex_cn: 流行音乐是主流的一部分。
words.en: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional.

words.ex: Birds begin migration in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在秋天开始迁徙。
words.en: The movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, especially regularly according to the seasons.

words.tr: adj. 有动机的；有积极性的； v. 激发；“motivate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is motivated to study hard for the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他有动力努力为考试学习。
words.en: If you are motivated by something, especially a strong emotion, it causes you to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.ex: The newcomer joined our class last week.
words.ex_cn: 这个新来的人上周加入了我们的班级。
words.en: A newcomer is a person who has recently arrived in a place or started an activity.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: His personality is very friendly and outgoing.
words.ex_cn: 他的个性非常友好和外向。
words.en: The combination of characteristics or qualities that form an individual's distinctive character.

words.ex: The prospect of a better job makes him happy.
words.ex_cn: 更好工作的前景让他感到高兴。
words.en: A prospect is the possibility that something will happen, or a view of a wide area.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: The rain will retard the construction of the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会延迟道路的建设。
words.en: To retard something means to delay it or make it happen more slowly than it would otherwise.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.tr: n. 半挂车；（一侧与其他建筑相连的）半独立式的住宅
words.ex: The truck driver parked the semi near the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 卡车司机把半挂车停在了仓库附近。
words.en: A semi is a trailer that is attached to the back of a truck and is used for transporting goods.

words.ex: The settler built a house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位定居者在河边建了一所房子。
words.en: A settler is a person who moves to a new place with the intention of staying there, especially in a previously uninhabited or sparsely inhabited area.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.tr: n. 社会学家；社会学者；
words.ex: The sociologist studied how people live in cities.
words.ex_cn: 这位社会学家研究了人们在城市中的生活方式。
words.en: A sociologist is someone who studies or is an expert in sociology, which is the study of society and social behavior.

words.tr: adj. 造成创伤的；痛苦的；不愉快的
words.ex: The car accident was a traumatic experience.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次创伤性的经历。
words.en: If something is traumatic, it causes you severe emotional distress and anxiety.

words.tr: adj. 想不到的；意料之外的；
words.ex: The rain was unexpected.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨是意想不到的。
words.en: If an event or someone's behaviour is unexpected, it surprises you because you were not expecting it to happen or because you did not think that person would behave in that way.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.ex: His conceit makes him ignore others' advice.
words.ex_cn: 他的自负让他忽视别人的建议。
words.en: An excessively favorable opinion of one's own abilities or worth; vanity.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.ex: He showed great concentration while solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解这道数学题时非常专注。
words.en: Concentration is the ability to focus all your attention on one thing without being distracted.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.ex: The boy's delinquency worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的犯罪行为让他的父母很担心。
words.en: Delinquency refers to minor crimes, especially those committed by young people.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；勇敢的； v. “dare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He made a daring jump off the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 他大胆地从桥上跳了下去。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as daring, you mean that they are willing to do things which might be dangerous or which might shock or anger other people.

words.ex: He is incapable of solving simple math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他无法解决简单的数学问题。
words.en: If someone is incapable of doing something, they are unable to do it.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.tr:
n. 担忧；关注；
v. 涉及；
words.ex: His main concern is his child's safety.
words.ex_cn: 他主要的担忧是孩子的安全。
words.en: If something concerns you, it worries you or causes you to feel anxious.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.tr:
adj. 不能治愈的；无可救药的
n. 患不治之症者；不能治愈的人
words.ex: The disease is incurable.
words.ex_cn: 这种病无法治愈。
words.en: If someone has an incurable disease, they cannot be cured of it.

words.tr:
adj. 就职的；开幕的；创立的
n. 就职演说
words.ex: He gave his inaugural speech last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚发表了就职演讲。
words.en: An inaugural event or speech is the first in a series planned to celebrate or introduce something.

words.ex: He chose teaching as his vocation.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了教学作为自己的职业。
words.en: A vocation is a type of work that you feel you are especially suited to do and to which you give much of your time and energy.

words.ex: His profession is a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的职业是教师。
words.en: A profession is a type of job that requires advanced education or training.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.ex: The soil is too infertile to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地太贫瘠了，无法种植庄稼。
words.en: Infertile land or soil is not able to produce good crops or plants. An infertile person, animal, or plant cannot have babies, eggs, or seeds.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.ex: The old machine is inefficient and uses too much energy.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器效率低，耗能太多。
words.en: If someone or something is inefficient, they do not use time, energy, or resources in the best way.

words.tr: v. 缩写；“abbreviate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: They abbreviated the word 'telephone' to 'phone'.
words.ex_cn: 他们把'telephone'这个单词缩写成'phone'。
words.en: Shortened in duration or extent; made briefer.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.tr: n. 广告活动；广告业； v. 做广告；“advertise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company launched a new advertising campaign last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月推出了一项新的广告活动。
words.en: The activity of producing advertisements for commercial products or services.

words.tr: n. （无线电和电视的）节目制作和播放； v. “broadcast”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company works in broadcasting TV shows.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司从事电视节目的制作和播放。
words.en: The transmission of programs or information by radio or television.

words.ex: Reading books can broaden your mind.
words.ex_cn: 读书可以扩大你的视野。
words.en: If something broadens or if you broaden it, it increases in size or range.

words.ex: He was born a commoner but rose to become a respected leader.
words.ex_cn: 他出身平民，但最终成为受人尊敬的领袖。
words.en: A commoner is someone who is not of noble rank.

words.tr: v. 限制；“confine”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 被限制的；狭窄的；
words.ex: He was confined to his room for a week.
words.ex_cn: 他被限制在房间里一周。
words.en: If something is confined to a particular place, it exists only in that place. If it is confined to a particular group, only the members of that group have it.

words.tr: adv. 大幅度地；相当地；很大地；
words.ex: The price has increased considerably.
words.ex_cn: 价格大幅上涨了。
words.en: To a notably large or significant extent.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The teacher gave a descriptive answer about the painting.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这幅画给出了一个描述性的回答。
words.en: If you describe something as descriptive, you mean that it gives a detailed account of something.

words.tr: adj. 有辨别力的；能洞悉的；眼光敏锐的； v. “discern”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a discerning shopper who always finds the best quality.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有辨别力的购物者，总是能找到最好的质量。
words.en: If you describe someone as discerning, you mean that they are able to judge which things of a particular kind are good and which are bad.

words.tr:
n. 日食；月食；黯然失色
v. 使失色
words.ex: We watched the solar eclipse last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚观看了日食。
words.en: An eclipse occurs when one celestial body moves into the shadow of another, temporarily obscuring it or cutting off its light.

words.ex: The cows graze in the enclosure.
words.ex_cn: 奶牛在围场里吃草。
words.en: An enclosure is an area that is surrounded by a barrier or fence, often used to keep animals in or to protect something.

words.ex: They called him 'Quick Feet' as an epithet.
words.ex_cn: 他们用‘快脚’作为他的绰号。
words.en: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase added to or substituted for a person's name, often to describe a characteristic or quality.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.tr:
n. 功能；职责；
v. 起作用；
words.ex: The function of this button is to turn on the light.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮的功能是打开灯。
words.en: A function is the purpose that something is designed to have or the job that someone is employed to do. It can also refer to a mathematical relationship or a social event.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.ex: The gravity of Earth pulls objects down.
words.ex_cn: 地球的重力把物体往下拉。
words.en: Gravity is the force that causes things to fall towards the Earth or towards any other physical body having mass.

words.ex: The helicopter flew over the city.
words.ex_cn: 直升机飞过了城市。
words.en: A helicopter is a type of aircraft that derives both lift and propulsion from one or more sets of horizontally revolving overhead rotors. It is capable of moving vertically and horizontally, the direction of motion being controlled by the pitch of the rotor blades.

words.ex: I saw him yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天看见他了。
words.en: You use him to refer to a man, boy, or male animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified.

words.ex: The chickens sleep in the henhouse at night.
words.ex_cn: 鸡晚上在鸡舍里睡觉。
words.en: A henhouse is a small building where chickens are kept.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.ex: He spoke without hesitation.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不犹豫地说了。
words.en: Hesitation is the act of pausing before doing something, especially because you are nervous or not certain about it.

words.ex: Bears hibernate in winter to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 熊在冬天冬眠以保存能量。
words.en: To spend the winter in a dormant state.

words.ex: He keeps his tools on the hob.
words.ex_cn: 他把工具放在炉灶台上。
words.en: A hob is a flat metal shelf at the side or back of a fireplace, where things can be placed to keep them warm.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.ex: He is informing his friends about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他正在通知他的朋友们关于这次会议。
words.en: If you inform someone about something, you tell them about it.

words.ex: The inventive child made a toy from cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个有创造力的孩子用纸板做了一个玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as inventive, you mean that they are good at inventing things or have clever and original ideas.

words.ex: He is a maker of wooden chairs.
words.ex_cn: 他是木椅的制造者。
words.en: A maker is a person or company that makes or produces something.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: He is merely a student.
words.ex_cn: 他仅仅是个学生。
words.en: You use merely to emphasize that something is only what you say and not better, more important, or more exciting.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: He chose an occupational therapy course.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了一门职业治疗课程。
words.en: Relating to a job or profession.

words.ex: He will participate in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧演出。
words.en: To take part in an activity or event.

words.ex: His last name is a patronymic from his father's name.
words.ex_cn: 他的姓氏来自他父亲的名字。
words.en: A patronymic is a name derived from the name of a father or ancestor, typically by the addition of a prefix or suffix.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: He will perform the task tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会执行这个任务。
words.en: To perform means to carry out, accomplish, or fulfill an action, task, or function. It can also refer to the act of presenting a form of entertainment, such as a play, concert, or other artistic expression, before an audience.

words.ex: The village by the lake is picturesque.
words.ex_cn: 湖边的村庄如画般美丽。
words.en: A picturesque place is attractive and interesting, especially in a way that is old-fashioned or unusual.

words.ex: He wrote a poetic poem with poetic words.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首充满诗意的诗。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of poetry or poets; having the qualities of poetry.

words.ex: He has possession of the keys.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有这些钥匙。
words.en: The state of having, owning, or controlling something.
